In respect of the accident which occurred on 2015, the claimant filed a claim petition contending that he had suffered a fracture of the anterior vertebral body, right pneumohemothorax with lung contusion and sternal body fracture.

The Tribunal on assessing the evidence has come to the conclusion that the claimant had suffered a whole disability of 8% and after adopting the notional income of Rs.7,000/- has awarded a sum of Rs.3,32,500/-.
The Tribunal has also fastened the liability on the insurer.
As a result, both of the insurer as well as the claimant are in appeal.

2. As far as the appeal of the insurer is concerned, which is on the liability, it is noticed that the contention advanced by the insurer is that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the requisite endorsement to drive the offending vehicle and, therefore, it would not be liable.

In such cases where NC: 2024:KHC:51114 breach of policy conditions is pleaded, the only option available to the insurer is to pay the compensation and then proceed to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle in the light of the judgment rendered in Yallava's case1.
3. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and it is held that the insurer shall pay the compensation and then proceed recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
4. As far as disability is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 8%.
The doctor who was examined, though not the treated doctor, has stated that the whole body disability was to the extent of 20%.
5. Having regard to his evidence and also the fractures suffered by the claimant, it would be appropriate to treat the whole body disability at 15%.
New India Assurance Co.Ltd Vs. Yallavva and Anr.- ILR 2020 KAR 2239 NC: 2024:KHC:51114 6.

sentences.text: As far as income is concerned, the Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.7,000/-, since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.9,000/- for the accident of the year 2015, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/-.

7. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,91,600/- (Rs.9,000/- X 12 X 18 X 15%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
8.

The Tribunal has awarded some Rs.1,24,000/-
towards 'medical expenses' which is just and proper and is affirmed.

9. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards NC: 2024:KHC:51114 'pain and suffering' and Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.

10. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-

sentences.text: In my view, since the climate was hospitalized for 8 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'diet and conveyance and attendant charges'.
11. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as two months.
In my view, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as four months and award a sum of Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000/- X 4 months).
Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

As awarded As awarded Sl. Compensation under by the by this No. different Heads Tribunal Court (Rs.) (Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings 40,000/- 60,000/-
2. Loss of laid up period 14,000/- 36,000/-

5. and attendant charges 6.

Accordingly, the claimant is held entitled for  compensation of Rs.5,71,600/- as against Rs.3,32,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
13.

However, the claimant would not be entitled for interest for the delayed period as per order dated 09.12.2024.
14.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and thereafter shall recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
